overview: This one-page cross-reference sheet records a November 19, 1934 communication from Tokyo concerning zinc-ore smelting in Japan. It points researchers to file 711.4215 Air Pollution/568g for an instruction requesting information about Japanese practices for controlling sulphur fumes emitted as gas from smelter stacks.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on control of sulphur fumes from zinc smelters in Japan
subfiles.about: The sheet redirects researchers to another file containing an instruction about Japanese controls on sulphur-fume emissions from zinc-smelter stacks.
subfiles.summary: This filing note concerns the smelting of zinc ore in Japan and a request for information about measures used to control sulphur fumes discharged from smelter stacks. It directs the reader to document 568g in decimal file 711.4215, under Air Pollution, for the relevant instruction. The sheet identifies Tokyo as the source and dates the referenced communication November 19, 1934.

interest: Although it contains no substantive report, this cross-reference is useful evidence of early U.S. State Department interest in industrial air-pollution controls in Japan. Its reference to sulphur-fume abatement at zinc smelters may help historians trace environmental-health concerns and technical information gathering across different parts of the Department's decimal filing system.
